newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says concensus with US in health import row.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says concensus with US in health import row.

text.p: Taiwan's Board of Foreign Trade said on Monday it had reached concensus with the United States in a dispute over U.S. firms' access to the island's medical equipment market.

Board deputy director Tseng Lien-fung, speaking in Taipei, said bilateral negotiations in Washington over the past several days had reached concensus in the dispute but that final wording of an agreement was still being worked out.
"We are optimistic," Tseng told reporters when asked whether Taiwan could avert feared economic sanctions under U.S. fair trade laws.

Taiwan media have speculated that the island could face punishment under Section 301 of the U.S. Trade Act, which mandates retaliation against countries whose markets are, in the U.S. view, unfairly shielded from foreign competition.
"Final wording can be worked out by the end of today," Tseng said without further comment.

U.S. medical equipment makers have accused Taiwan's Health Insurance Bureau of unfairly dominating the island's market for medical equipment by applying quotas and mandating prices too low to allow fair compeition.
September 30 is a deadline for resolution of the dispute.

Taiwan negotiators have said that if Washington decides that Taiwan's national health care system is a monopoly impeding U.S. products, the U.S. government could place it on a Special 301 watch list of countries that engage in unfair trade.
Countries on the list are subject to an intensive investigation and If allegations are substantiated, punitive sanctions can be imposed.
